sentences.text: Zhengheornis is an early bird relative known as a member of the Avialae, a group containing modern birds and their closest relatives.
Studies indicate it shares a close evolutionary relationship with Yuezhuornis, forming a distinct family called Zhengheornithidae.
Fossils were found between March and April 2024 near Yangyuan Village in Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.
The holotype — the specific specimen used to define the species — is kept at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology with the number IVPP V34168.
Zhengheornis offers evidence that the shortening of vertebrae happened before the fusion of the pygostyle — a fused tail structure — in the stepwise evolution of the bird tail.
Phylogenetic analysis places Zhengheornis within Avialae, diverging after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx but before Baminornis.
This animal lived during the Late Jurassic, specifically at the boundary between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages approximately 150 million years ago.
Its time range is estimated to span from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
The remains were discovered in the Nanyuan Formation, which represents a primarily swamp-like environment.
The exact position of Zhengheornis relative to Anchiornithidae, Archaeopteryx, and Baminornis remains a subject of phylogenetic reconstruction.
